bull_case: Lilly is defining the obesity/diabetes treatment standard through tirzepatide and a successor incretin platform, while global manufacturing expansion and adjacent therapeutic areas extend the structural runway.
bear_case: The franchise is highly concentrated in cardiometabolic demand. Pricing, reimbursement, safety or superior rival drugs could compress the economics of several headline products at once.
thesis: LLY is a structural leader in metabolic medicine. Tirzepatide has shifted obesity treatment into a mainstream pharmaceutical category, and orforglipron/retatrutide extend the platform. Leadership is reinforced by manufacturing scale and global distribution. Durability is lower than headline growth because cardiometabolic products are ~80% of Q2 revenue; oncology is the only other therapeutic area above 10%, leaving meaningful common-factor concentration.

evidence.claim: Q2 2026 cardiometabolic revenue was $18.353B of $22.974B total revenue, led by Mounjaro $9.943B and Zepbound $4.928B.
Q2 oncology revenue was $2.570B, about 11.2% of total revenue, providing a second independent final market above the rubric's 10% threshold.
Orforglipron was FDA-approved for obesity and retatrutide Phase 3 obesity and type 2 diabetes programs met primary endpoints, extending Lilly's metabolic leadership beyond tirzepatide.
Lilly is investing globally in manufacturing capacity, including an additional $4.5B Indiana commitment announced with Q2 results, to support current and prospective medicines.

counterevidence: Cardiometabolic health represented roughly 80% of Q2 revenue.
Novo Nordisk and other large pharmaceutical firms can fund competing incretins and novel obesity mechanisms.
Payer reimbursement and government pricing can alter category economics even when clinical demand remains strong.
Manufacturing intensity creates physical execution risk not present in asset-light platforms.
unknowns: Long-run obesity-treatment penetration at reimbursed prices.
Commercial overlap among tirzepatide, orforglipron and retatrutide.
Whether oncology or immunology can become another >10% independent demand pool.
falsifiers: Lilly loses meaningful metabolic share without an offsetting successor product.
Successor incretins mostly cannibalize Lilly's existing franchise without expanding patients or economics.
Oncology and other non-metabolic businesses shrink while the metabolic franchise faces common pricing or safety pressure.

key_kpis.name: Cardiometabolic share / growth
key_kpis.threshold: retain category leadership without dependence on price inflation

key_kpis.name: Non-metabolic revenue pools
key_kpis.threshold: maintain at least one second >10% independent therapeutic market

subscores.rationale: Obesity and metabolic treatment is undergoing a durable clinical and demand shift, with multiple molecules and indications supporting a 5-10 year runway.
Lilly is defining efficacy, product-form and manufacturing standards in the current incretin market at very large commercial scale.
Two independent therapeutic final markets exceed 10% of revenue—cardiometabolic and oncology—mapping to the observable score of 75. Metabolic concentration remains high.

uncertainties.rationale: Demand is established; future reimbursement and competitive intensity determine monetization.
Commercial and pipeline leadership is directly visible.
A common metabolic pricing, reimbursement or safety shock would affect most current revenue.
